summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, morbid obesity, and a Port-A-Cath due to difficult venous access was admitted for acute-on-chronic epigastric pain. She presented with leukocytosis (WBC 24.9) and hyperglycemia (glucose 453), but imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology. Blood cultures drawn from her port grew multiple coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species, prompting Infectious Disease consultation and treatment with daptomycin. She remained afebrile, and repeat blood cultures were negative. Her abdominal pain improved significantly after bowel movements, consistent with chronic functional GI issues. She was discharged home on a 10-day course of outpatient daptomycin with home health support, Benadryl premedication, and instructions to monitor blood glucose and maintain bowel regularity.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter, initial encounter
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic (poly)neuropathy
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
